title: Jülich Supercomputing Centre Benchmark Evaluates Quantum Error Correction Primitives Across Quantinuum, IBM, and IQM Hardware
source_used: Quantum Computing Report (full text read, citing the JSC study)
key_facts: Researchers at Germany's Jülich Supercomputing Centre (JSC) published a benchmark study of quantum error correction (QEC) primitives: mid-circuit measurement, qubit reset, dynamic feed-forward control and spectator idling.
The study tested ten commercial quantum processors from Quantinuum, IBM and IQM.
The study is titled 'Evaluating the performance of QEC primitives on quantum processors at large width and depth' and is posted as arXiv:2610.05928.
Quantinuum's trapped-ion systems showed the strongest overall performance across the tested primitives, with a signal clarity of r = 0.733 on a 91-data-qubit triangular colour code.
On an 11-patch surface-code memory experiment on IBM's ibm_phoenix, the benchmark correlated with logical error survival at 0.83 to 0.88.
The benchmark is the authors' own low-sampling test (LR-QAOA) mapped onto surface, colour and qLDPC codes.
quote_evidence: According to the findings, Quantinuum’s trapped-ion systems demonstrated the strongest overall performance across the tested QEC primitives.
A benchmark study published by researchers at Germany’s Jülich Supercomputing Centre (JSC) has evaluated key Quantum Error Correction (QEC) primitives
why_it_matters_hint: An early research comparison of commercial quantum processors on error-fixing tasks; a preprint with no outside review reported.
notes: Full text read on QCR. arXiv preprint; no peer review reported. Pool score 5 kept.
